tout

TOWT (rhymes with 'shout') -- from Middle English tuten ('to peer, look out'). · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To tout is to aggressively promote or praise something, especially in order to sell it.

At the school fair, the sixth-grade club continually touted its bake-sale brownies as 'guaranteed to sell out by noon,' even on the two days they didn't.

Worked Example

The startup's CEO never stopped touting his app as 'the future of grocery shopping,' even to strangers waiting in line at the grocery store.

Notice tout is almost always about publicly, energetically talking something up -- a product, a plan, a candidate -- usually with an eye toward selling it or winning support, not quietly recommending it in private.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

hype: To hype something is to pump it up with exaggerated, excited praise — the claim itself gets inflated. Touting is about the pushing, not the inflating: a company can tout its safety record all day using perfectly true numbers. Hype stretches the message; touting hammers on it.

pitch: To pitch is to make a focused sales presentation to a particular listener — you pitch an idea to investors and wait for a yes or no. Touting is broader and louder: praising something to anyone who will listen, again and again, with no single decision on the table.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

downplay: to make something seem less important than it is

disparage: to speak of something in a negative or dismissive way

Where it sits · how aggressively the praise is pushed — promote → tout → hawk

promote vs. tout: Promote is the calm, neutral base of the scale — a sponsor can promote a fun run simply by listing it on a website — while to tout is to push the praise aggressively, hammering the sales talk at everyone within earshot.

hawk vs. tout: Hawk pushes past even touting: a vendor hawking sunglasses is in your path, shouting prices and waving the goods, where touting is aggressive praise that still stops short of chasing customers down the street.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — tout-

root — tout-: to peer, look out, keep watch (Middle English (tuten))

Put it together

Put it together: Tout began as a Middle English word for peering or looking out -- picture a lookout scanning the street for customers. That watching-for-buyers sense gradually shifted into today's meaning: loudly talking something up to attract attention and sales.

Use the root in a new word: touter

Use the root in a new word: touter: A racecourse touter used to make a living tipping off gamblers about which horse was supposedly guaranteed to win.
